summary: Iteration 4 — printable PDF report fully verified. Added /app/backend/tests/test_pdf_report.py (26 tests, all passing) covering: happy path for all four instruments (200, application/pdf, %PDF- header, Content-Disposition attachment filename 'ratherknow-<slug>-<8hex>.pdf'); auth matrix (401 no token, 403 other user, 404 unknown session, 409 not-complete); content correctness via pymupdf text extraction (instrument name, tier chip word from locked register, tier statement text, reader name, algo_version 'rk-1.0.0', safety floor, helpline 0808 2000 247, locked disclaimer in footer); forbidden-claims audit (no 'diagnosis', no numeric compatibility %, only negated 'compatibility score' mentions inside the 'What this document is not' block, only negated 'percentile' mention on closeness inside the norms-don't-exist-yet negation); closeness shows 'of 7' raw values with no band/percentile; PDF numbers match GET /result exactly for essential delta overall, eq overall score, all 15 personality factor stens (≥60% coincidence check across parsed tokens), and both closeness dimension values; situation framing: three users (single_dating, in_relationship, post_breakup) on the same essential answer vector produce IDENTICAL numbers but DIFFERENT framing sentences (signature phrases isolated to their own PDFs — no cross-leak); edge cases render without failure — all-1s and all-5s essential (1-4 pages), personality with all-5s that trips the social-desirability / central-tendency validity chips (still renders, 'Validity indices' block present); delta wording direction verified against sign of delta.per_archetype (positive => 'you want more of this than you are', negative => 'you are more of this than you want'). Full regression: 70/70 backend tests green (`python -m pytest backend/tests -o addopts=''`), tests/test_locked_copy.py -> 'LOCKED COPY OK', tests/_e2e_test.py -> 'PACKAGED E2E OK'. Frontend Playwright verified the DownloadReport card: on a completed closeness result page /results/{sid}, data-testid=download-report is present, data-testid=download-report-btn triggers a real .pdf download whose filename starts 'ratherknow-closeness-mirror' and whose bytes begin with '%PDF'; no download-report-error was rendered. Confirmed the card is NOT present on the Flag Check reflection pages (/reflection/{id}, /flag-check/{id}) — Flag Check stays unscored with no printable report, as specified.
critical_code_review_comments: report_pdf.py `_essential` correctly maps sign to wording: `v > 0` (ideal higher than self) -> 'you want more of this than you are'; `v < 0` -> 'you are more of this than you want'. This matches the code comment in the review request and was verified against real per_archetype signs on two extreme fixtures (self=1/ideal=5 and self=5/ideal=1).

The report is rendered from `session['result']` only and never touches the scorer — good. `_score_*` functions are unreachable from the PDF path; GET /report.pdf pulls the immutable snapshot and reuses it, so numbers cannot drift from /result.

situation_note() falls through to None when situation or instrument is unknown, and the PDF cleanly omits the 'Read for where you are' block in that case — no crash, no empty header. Verified by running against random-answer situations.

Content-Disposition uses fixed slugs derived from INSTRUMENTS[key]['name'].lower().replace(' ', '-') — stable across releases; filename hex uses session_id[:8], not the whole UUID, which is friendlier and still keeps a per-download identifier.

Closeness PDF explicitly states 'No band or percentile is shown, because the norms to justify one do not exist yet.' — satisfies the hard-rule requirement and was asserted. Values render as '4.0 of 7' etc. with no misleading banding.
Locked disclaimer, safety headline+floor, and attribution are pulled from LOCKED (locked_copy.json) verbatim; no re-typed copies. Hash-tested via tests/test_locked_copy.py — still passing.
Report footer prints 'Page N · scored under rk-1.0.0' — this is the algo_version pulled from the stored result, so an older result would still stamp its original version (immutability by design).

Small refinement idea (not a bug): the closeness PDF's confidence label ('Low', 'Moderate', 'High') is capitalised with .title(); if 'unknown' ever reaches this branch it prints 'Unknown' with a trailing period from the following sentence — harmless but worth a NBSP guard if that state becomes user-visible.

DownloadReport.js swallows the real error message ('The report couldn't be built. Try again in a moment.') — fine for UX, but a `console.error(err)` in the catch would help debugging without changing copy.

test_credentials: test.user@ratherknow.com / knowmore123 (post_breakup) — unchanged. Iteration 4 tests use throwaway TEST_pdf_* / TEST_ui_* users created per-run.
seed_data_creation: Backend tests create ~7 TEST_ prefixed throwaway users (post_breakup / single_dating / in_relationship) plus one completed session per instrument per user. All keyed TEST_ for cleanup. UI test creates one further TEST_ui_* user and one completed closeness session.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `python -m pytest backend/tests -o addopts=''` for the full 70-test regression (auth 16 + iteration3 13 + mirror_v2 15 + pdf_report 26). test_pdf_report.py uses pymupdf to extract PDF text; wrapped-line phrases inside table cells (e.g. 'you want more of this than you are' when the value column is 100.0 pts) need whitespace-normalisation via re.sub(r'\s+',' ', text) before substring assertions — pymupdf inserts \n at wrap points. Situation-framing signatures are pinned via short phrases (e.g. 'window after an ending is short and unusually clear') rather than importing the notes module, which keeps the test rootpath-agnostic. The closeness bar table renders values as '4.0 of 7' with the sublabel column carrying the 'of 7' string — do not treat 'of 7' as a numeric assertion. INSTRUMENT_META maps 'closeness' via key 'MI-AS-36' from the stored result (that's the instrument string in Mongo), while the URL/frontend uses 'closeness' — the filename slug goes through INSTRUMENTS[key]['name'] so the mapping is consistent.
rca of the issue: N/A — no product bugs surfaced. Two initial test-authoring issues: (1) the reader name in the PDF kicker is uppercased via `.upper()` in report_pdf.py — asserting the mixed-case name failed until I did a case-insensitive check; (2) reportlab wraps long paragraph cells, which causes pymupdf to insert a newline mid-phrase; normalising whitespace before the substring assertion fixed the delta-wording direction test. Neither is a product bug.
